chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra'ib, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a Christian woman who was married to a Christian, and he divorced her. Is there a waiting period upon her similar to the waiting period of a Muslim woman? He said: No, because the People of the Book are slaves (in domain) of the Imam. Do you not see that they pay the Jizya to him just as the slave pays the tribute to his master? He said: And whoever from them embraces Islam, he is free, and the Jizya is dropped from him.

I said: So what is her waiting period if a Muslim man intends to marry her? He said: Her waiting period is the waiting period of a slave woman, two menstruations, or forty-five days, before she becomes Muslim. I said to him: And if she becomes Muslim after he has divorced her? He said: If she becomes Muslim after he has divorced her, then her waiting period is the waiting period of a Muslim woman.

I said: And if he dies from her, and she is a Christian and he is a Christian, and a man from the Muslims intends to marry her? He said: The Muslim man cannot marry her until she observes the waiting period from the Christian, of four months and ten days, which is the waiting period of a Muslim woman whose husband has died.

I said to him: How is it that when she is divorced her waiting period is that of a slave woman, and her waiting period when her husband dies from her is that of a free Muslim woman, while you mention that they are slaves of the Imam? He said: Her waiting period in divorce is not like her waiting period when her husband dies from her.

Then he said: Indeed, the slave woman and the free woman, both of them, when their husband dies from them, are equal in the waiting period, except that the free woman observes mourning (Iddah with restriction) and the slave woman does not observe mourning.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a Christian woman divorced by a Christian or widowed by a Christian according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential nuance that Ahl al-Kitab women are considered 'slaves' (mawali) of the Imam specifically regarding the payment of Jizya, a status that dictates their shorter waiting period (Iddah) of two menstruations upon divorce. It further clarifies the distinction between the waiting period for death versus divorce, noting that while the duration differs based on marital status and conversion, the fundamental principle of their subordinate legal standing in personal status law remains consistent with Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ra’ib, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a Christian woman who was under (married to) a Christian.

So he divorced her. Is there a waiting period upon her similar to what is upon the Muslim woman?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, because the People of the Book are in the domain of the Imam<sup>asws</sup>. Do you not see that they are paying the taxation to him<sup>asws</sup> just as the slave pays whatever he earns to his master?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the one who becomes a Muslim from them, so he is free. The taxation would be dropped from him.

I said, ‘So what is her waiting period if the Muslim man intends to marry her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Her waiting period is a waiting period of the slave woman, two menstruations, or forty-five days, before she became a Muslim’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Supposing she becomes a Muslim after her divorce?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she becomes a Muslim after her divorce, so her waiting period is a waiting period of the Muslim woman’.

I said, ‘Supposing he dies from her, and she is a Christian and he is a Christian, so a man from the Muslims intends to marry her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Muslim man cannot marry her until she observes the waiting period from the Christian, of four months and ten (days), being a waiting period of the Muslim woman widowed from her husband’.

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How did it become, when she is divorced her waiting period is that of the slave girl, and her waiting period became, when her husband dies from her, a waiting period of the free Muslim woman, and you<sup>asws</sup> mentioned that they are in the domain of the Imam<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Her waiting period regarding the divorce is not like her waiting period when he husband dies from her’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The slave girls, and the free women, both of them are equal, when their husbands die from them, with regards to the waiting period, except that the free woman would limit herself (in mourning), and the slave girl would not limit herself (in mourning)’.
